dfItems.name: Product / SKU eVar
dfItems.approach: Product field in the Commerce XDM field group
dfItems.rationale: Commerce field group is purpose-built for product-level detail and arrives pre-mapped for most standard commerce events.

dfItems.name: Order ID eVar
dfItems.approach: Order ID in Commerce XDM field group
dfItems.rationale: Maps directly; used as the join key for order-level metrics and de-duplication.

dfItems.name: Campaign / tracking code eVar
dfItems.rationale: Standard field; also feeds Attribution IQ once multiple touches are captured.

dfItems.name: Page Name prop
dfItems.rationale: Direct mapping; populated automatically by the Web SDK.

dfItems.name: Site Section prop
dfItems.rationale: Direct mapping; useful for building Data View rollups by section.

dfItems.name: Custom conversion eVar (business-specific)
dfItems.rationale: Business-specific values need a schema extension designed and named deliberately; this is where most implementation time goes.
dfItems.prereqs: Schema design workshop; Field naming convention agreed

dfItems.name: Marketing Cloud Visitor ID (ECID)
dfItems.rationale: ECID carries over directly and remains the anonymous backbone identity.

dfItems.name: CRM ID / Customer ID (server-side)
dfItems.rationale: Needs a registered identity namespace and a decision on stitching priority relative to ECID.
dfItems.prereqs: Identity namespace registered; Stitching priority defined

dfItems.name: Success Event: Orders
dfItems.rationale: Standard commerce event; count and revenue metrics available immediately in Workspace.

dfItems.name: Success Event: Cart Adds
dfItems.rationale: Direct mapping; also the building block for cart-abandonment segments.

dfItems.name: Success Event: custom conversion (e.g. signup)
dfItems.rationale: Straightforward to add, but needs a name and owner agreed so it isn't duplicated later.

dfItems.name: Processing Rules (VISTA)
dfItems.rationale: Logic that used to live in Processing Rules moves upstream into Data Prep at ingestion; this is a rebuild, not a copy.
dfItems.prereqs: Audit of active Processing Rules; Data Prep mapping designed

dfItems.name: Classifications (SAINT)
dfItems.approach: Lookup dataset joined via Data Prep, or schema field enrichment
dfItems.rationale: SAINT classifications don't migrate automatically; they become a lookup dataset or a richer upstream field.

dfItems.name: Segments
dfItems.rationale: CJA adds a Person container, so most AA visitor-scoped segments become simpler and more accurate as Person-scoped segments.

dfItems.name: Calculated Metrics
dfItems.approach: Derived Fields / Calculated Metrics in Data View
dfItems.rationale: Formula logic is broadly the same concept, but component references and containers differ enough to require a rebuild, not an export/import.

dfItems.name: Virtual Report Suites (roll-ups)
dfItems.rationale: One Connection can power several Data Views, replacing the need for many narrow report suites.

dfItems.name: Cross-Device Analysis (if used in AA)
dfItems.rationale: True cross-device stitching at scale typically requires Real-Time CDP alongside CJA, not CJA alone.
dfItems.prereqs: Identity graph strategy; Consent model for stitching

dfItems.name: Media / Video tracking (Heartbeat)
dfItems.rationale: Media Analytics has a dedicated schema and its own Data View best practices; plan it as its own workstream.

dfItems.name: Mobile app data (AppMeasurement SDK)
dfItems.approach: Mobile via Edge Network / AEP Mobile SDK
dfItems.rationale: Legacy AppMeasurement SDK is replaced by the Edge-based Mobile SDK; app teams need lead time here.

dfItems.name: Offline / CRM batch upload
dfItems.rationale: Offline data becomes a first-class dataset joinable to digital behavior: a genuinely new capability, not just a migration.
dfItems.prereqs: Source system connector available; Batch cadence agreed

dfItems.name: Marketing channel attribution (last-touch)
dfItems.rationale: Multi-touch attribution across channels is native to CJA Workspace: a step up from last-touch marketing channel reporting in AA.
dfItems.prereqs: Channel taxonomy agreed; Attribution model selected

dfItems.name: Anomaly detection (Analysis Workbench)
dfItems.rationale: Conceptually similar; needs to be reconfigured against the new metrics once parity is reached.

dfItems.name: Data Warehouse / FTP exports
dfItems.rationale: SQL-based access to raw event-level data replaces flat-file warehouse exports, and is far more flexible.

dfItems.name: Debugger / validation tooling
dfItems.rationale: Replaces the AA/Launch debugger for validating data collection in real time during rebuild.

segments.name: Started, didn't finish
segments.description: People who added something to their cart but never completed the purchase.
segments.aaLogic: Sequential container: hit with Cart Add event, then Exclude hit with Order event, within N days, usually scoped to Visit or Visitor.
segments.cjaLogic: Person container in CJA evaluates this across every channel and device tied to that identity, not just the session or browser where the cart add happened.

segments.name: High-value / high-loyalty customers
segments.description: Your best customers, measured by how much they've bought or how loyal they've been.
segments.aaLogic: Visitor-scoped container using count of Purchase events and a revenue threshold; accuracy depends on how well devices are stitched to one visitor.
segments.cjaLogic: Person container aggregates every identity (web, app, in-person/CRM) into one lifetime view, so the threshold reflects the whole relationship, not one device's slice of it.

segments.name: Multi-channel engaged
segments.description: People who interact with you across more than one channel or device.
segments.aaLogic: Sequential container across two report suites or a cross-device solution add-on, often approximate and hard to validate.
segments.cjaLogic: Native cross-dataset, cross-channel sequencing once identities are stitched: no add-on required, and it's auditable at the event level.

segments.name: Engaged with content, didn't convert
segments.description: People who read, watched, or browsed content but took no further action.
segments.aaLogic: Sequential container: hit with content page view ≥2 times, Exclude hit with conversion event, same Visit.
segments.cjaLogic: Same logic, but can span visits and channels via the Person container, catching converters who came back on a different device.

segments.name: Churn / lapse risk
segments.description: Customers whose activity has dropped off compared to their usual pattern.
segments.aaLogic: Visitor container comparing recent activity to a historical baseline, usually built and maintained as a saved segment with manual date-range updates.
segments.cjaLogic: Same pattern, but can be paired with a Derived Field for recency and refreshed automatically; often layered with Intelligent Alerts.

segments.name: Campaign responders
segments.description: People who clicked, opened, or otherwise responded to a specific campaign.
segments.aaLogic: Hit-level container filtering on tracking code / campaign eVar, sequential to a conversion event.
segments.cjaLogic: Same idea, strengthened by Attribution IQ so response can be credited across every touch, not just last-touch.

segments.name: Recent service / support interaction
segments.description: Customers who've recently contacted support or opened a service case.
segments.aaLogic: Difficult in AA: usually requires a separate classification import, or not modeled at all.
segments.cjaLogic: A joinable dataset (e.g. CRM case data) becomes just another event stream in the Person container: a genuinely new capability for most AA implementations.

segments.name: New vs. returning
segments.description: Distinguishes first-time visitors from people who've been here before.
segments.aaLogic: Visitor container using 'First Visit' segment or a new/returning dimension set at the hit level.
segments.cjaLogic: Same logic, made more reliable because 'returning' is evaluated against the full stitched identity rather than a device-scoped visitor ID.

identityStages.name: No stitching
identityStages.enables: Aggregate, channel-siloed reporting. Each device/browser is its own identity.
identityStages.prereqs: None. This is the default state most AA implementations start from
identityStages.blockers: No shared login/CRM ID captured in digital properties; No identity namespace strategy defined

identityStages.name: Deterministic login stitch
identityStages.enables: Person-level view whenever a customer is logged in or identifiable: the foundation for real segmentation.
identityStages.prereqs: CRM/customer ID captured at login and sent to Edge Network; Identity namespace registered in AEP
identityStages.blockers: Login events not consistently instrumented across properties; No agreement on which ID 'wins' when both exist

identityStages.name: Cross-channel deterministic + probabilistic
identityStages.enables: Segments and metrics that span web, app, offline purchase and service interactions for the same person.
identityStages.prereqs: Mobile SDK and offline sources connected; Probabilistic matching enabled where deterministic IDs are missing
identityStages.blockers: Offline data not yet flowing into AEP; Data governance sign-off on probabilistic matching

identityStages.name: Unified identity graph
identityStages.enables: Activation-ready profiles: true cross-device journeys, real-time triggers, and consent-aware suppression at the identity level.
identityStages.prereqs: Real-Time CDP provisioned; Consent management integrated into the identity graph
identityStages.blockers: Typically the last stage reached; most orgs plan for this rather than start here

governance.name: Data Governance Labels
governance.description: Sensitivity labels (e.g. contractual, identity-linked, sensitive) applied to fields in the schema.
governance.example: A field holding health or financial sensitivity is labeled at the schema level, and that label travels with the data everywhere it's used.
governance.mechanism: Enforced by Adobe Experience Platform at the field level: usage is blocked automatically in downstream tools, not just documented in a policy.

governance.name: Access Control Groups / Sandboxes
governance.description: Who can see which datasets, Data Views and sandboxes.
governance.example: A regional marketing team gets access to their sandbox and Data Views only, separate from the global analytics team's production sandbox.
governance.mechanism: Managed in Adobe Admin Console via Product Profiles, scoped per sandbox.

governance.name: Data Usage Labels
governance.description: Contractual or legal restrictions on how specific data can be used downstream (e.g. no use in targeted advertising).
governance.example: A dataset sourced under a contract that prohibits ad-targeting use carries a usage label that blocks it from activation flows.
governance.mechanism: Enforced by AEP's data usage policy engine at the point of activation.

governance.name: Consent & Identity Governance
governance.description: Opt-outs and consent preferences propagate to every identity tied to a person, not just one dataset.
governance.example: A customer opts out on the website; that preference is honored across app, email and offline touchpoints because it's tied to the identity graph.
governance.mechanism: Consent flags stored against the identity graph; checked before activation or export.

roles.name: Analyst
roles.from: Analysis Workbench, Report Builder, ad hoc segments scoped to one report suite.
roles.to: CJA Workspace with cross-channel Data Views, plus Query Service for SQL-level access to raw event data.
roles.newSkill: Thinking in Person vs. Event vs. Session containers, and when to use each.
roles.quickWin: The first rebuilt Data View usually answers a cross-channel question that was previously impossible, a good moment to demonstrate value early.

roles.name: Marketer / Campaign Manager
roles.from: Segments built and used inside Adobe Analytics, manually exported for activation.
roles.to: Segments built in CJA, activated directly into Real-Time CDP / Journey Optimizer without manual export.
roles.newSkill: Understanding that a Person-container segment already reflects every channel: no more stitching audiences by hand across tools.
roles.quickWin: Show a segment triggering an actual message send in the same workshop; the previously multi-day activation process becomes minutes.

roles.name: Data Engineer / Implementation
roles.from: s.tags / AppMeasurement, Processing Rules, SAINT classifications.
roles.to: Web/Mobile SDK on Edge Network, XDM schema design, Data Prep transformations, identity namespace management.
roles.newSkill: Schema design: this is the highest-leverage new skill on the team, since a well-designed schema saves rework across every other role.
roles.quickWin: Start schema design before any tag rebuild; it's the one artifact every other workstream depends on.

roles.name: IT / Governance Admin
roles.from: Report suite and user management in the AA Admin Console.
roles.to: Sandboxes, Product Profiles, data governance labels, and consent management in Experience Platform.
roles.newSkill: Designing a sandbox strategy up front (how many, who owns which); retrofitting this later is expensive.
roles.quickWin: Stand up a dev sandbox on day one so engineering can start schema work without touching production.

glossary.definition: The structured data model (Experience Data Model) that defines every field CJA can use. Think of it as the blueprint your data has to fit.
A way of scoping a segment or metric to everything tied to one person, across every device and channel, not just one session.
A way of scoping a segment or metric to a single event, the most granular level of detail.
A way of scoping a segment or metric to one visit, similar to a Visit container in Adobe Analytics.
Experience Cloud ID: the anonymous identifier Adobe uses to recognize a browser or device before someone logs in.
The map Adobe builds connecting every known identifier (ECID, CRM ID, mobile ID, and so on) back to one person.
The lens built on top of your data that determines which dimensions and metrics show up in Workspace.
The link between one or more datasets and your schema. One Connection can power several Data Views.
A calculated dimension built from other fields, similar in spirit to a classification or calculated dimension in Adobe Analytics.
A formula-based metric built from other metrics, the CJA equivalent of an Adobe Analytics calculated metric.
CJA's native multi-touch attribution feature, crediting conversions across every touchpoint instead of just the last one.
Adobe's platform for building and activating audiences in real time across channels.
The tool that maps and transforms incoming data into your XDM schema at the point of ingestion.
SQL-based access to the raw event data behind your Data Views, for advanced or custom analysis.
A layer for large-scale data engineering and preparation work directly inside Adobe Experience Platform.
Adobe Analytics' classification tool for enriching raw values, such as mapping a product SKU to a category.
Adobe Analytics' processing rules engine, used to transform data as it's collected.
Adobe's tool for orchestrating and delivering cross-channel customer journeys and messages.
Adobe's modern data collection infrastructure that replaces the legacy Adobe Analytics tracking server.
The current Adobe library for collecting web data and sending it to the Edge Network.
The current Adobe library for collecting app data and sending it to the Edge Network, replacing the legacy AppMeasurement SDK.
A registered category of identifier, such as an email address or CRM ID, that Adobe uses to stitch identities together.
The Adobe Admin Console mechanism for controlling which users can access which sandboxes, datasets, or Data Views.

Adobe Analytics' classic custom-value variable (short for 'extended variable'), used to capture things like product IDs, campaign codes, or order IDs. In CJA these become fields on your XDM schema instead.
Stock Keeping Unit: the unique code identifying a specific product, commonly captured in a Product eVar in Adobe Analytics.
Adobe Analytics' classic traffic variable (short for 'property'), used for things like page name or site section. In CJA these become standard fields, usually in the Web field group.
